title: Marketing mix (4Ps)
examples: What is the difference between product and service in the marketing mix?
Can you give an example of how promotion can change the price?
Why is the 'place' element so important for a local shop?

explain.say: The marketing mix helps businesses sell things well. It uses four main elements to help you.
Product means the actual item or service you offer. It must meet customer needs well.
Price is the amount of money customers pay for your product. It must cover costs and make profit.
Place is where the customer can actually buy your goods. Think about shops or websites.
Promotion tells people about your product. This includes advertising and sales events.
For a new brand of running shoes, the product is light and durable. The price is set high to show quality. The place is sold in sports shops. And promotion uses fitness influencers.

draw.text: Running Shoes: Product, Price, Place, Promo

faq.q: Does the marketing mix only apply to physical goods?
faq.a: No, it applies to services too. A haircut, for example, is a service that needs all four Ps.
asks: Can I use the 4Ps for non-physical things?

faq.q: If I change the product, do I also need to change the price?
faq.a: Usually, yes. A better product might allow you to charge a higher price point.
asks: How do product and price connect?

faq.a: No, 'Place' also includes online distribution channels. Think about your website being a place.

faq.q: What is the difference between advertising and promotion?
faq.a: Advertising is paid communication, like a TV ad. Promotion is a broader term including sales and PR.
asks: Is promotion the same as advertising?
What is the difference between the two?

faq.q: Can I ignore one of the 4Ps?
faq.a: It is very difficult to ignore any P. If you ignore one, your marketing mix will be unbalanced.
asks: Which P is the most important one?

facts: The marketing mix consists of Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.
Product refers to the goods or services offered to the market.
Price is the monetary value exchanged for the product.
Place relates to the channels used to get the product to the customer.

quiz.say: A company decides to make its product much more eco-friendly and durable. Which P is primarily being changed?
quiz.why: The question describes a change to the nature and quality of the item itself.

wrong.0: Changing the product might affect the price, but the change described is about the item, not the cost.
wrong.1: Changing the product does not automatically mean you need to change where it is sold.
wrong.2: Changing the product is a physical change, not a communication strategy.

quiz.say: A local bakery starts selling its bread online through a dedicated website. This change mainly affects which P?
quiz.why: Moving sales online changes the distribution channel, which is the definition of Place.

wrong.0: While they might advertise the website, the core change is in the selling location.
wrong.2: The bread itself has not changed, only how it is sold.
wrong.3: The question does not mention any change in the cost of the bread.

quiz.say: If a business raises its price significantly, they might need to adjust their advertising efforts. This shows a link between which two Ps?
quiz.why: A high price needs strong promotion to justify the cost to the customer.

wrong.0: While related, the immediate link described is between cost and communication.
wrong.1: This link is always present, but the question specifically mentions advertising efforts.
wrong.2: This link is about visibility, but the question focuses on the cost factor.
